rv.q: The adaptation packs all the joy of the animated movie and Matt West's production adds magic of its own.
All in all, it’s an extravagant, memorable update on a tale that’s as old as time, but as exhilarating as ever.
But once we are ensconced in the castle, Matt West’s production becomes a marvellous mix of ghostly thrills and pantomime laughs.

This being said, it is difficult to envision many theatregoers not enjoying this show, though it may have a small handful of dramaturgical drawbacks, it delivers on so many fronts with powerhouse performances, dazzling magical effects and awe inspiring company numbers.
Ultimately Beauty and the Beast hits all the marks you want from a heartwarming Disney show.
This new production freshens it up a bit while retaining the joy and magic that has made it such a fan favourite.
This current revival of the tale as old as time takes to the London stage, but sadly feels anchored somewhere within this uneven history.

cn.t: This faithful adaptation of the beloved Disney film delivers largely enchanting family entertainment with a vigorous Belle and magical production elements, though some critics find it uneven and anchored to the musical's middling theatrical history.
